questions.prompt: What is the structural formula of Water (H₂O)?
questions.explanation: The structural formula of Water (H₂O) is H — O — H.

questions.prompt: Which type of bond is formed when the nitrogen of ammonia donates its lone pair to the hydrogen of HCl?
questions.explanation: When the nitrogen of ammonia donates its lone pair to the hydrogen of HCl, a coordinate covalent bond is formed.

questions.prompt: Which one of these is a property of a metal?
questions.explanation: A metal has this property: Can be drawn into wires and sheets. (Section 3.6)

options: Mostly made of two or more non-metals
Dissolves in water and is hydrated by it
Can be drawn into wires and sheets

questions.prompt: What is the physical state of Hydrogen chloride (HCl) at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen chloride (HCl) is a gas at room temperature. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Why do atoms combine with other atoms to form chemical bonds?
questions.explanation: Atoms tend to decrease their energy by combining; this increases their stability.

options: To lose all of their electrons
To decrease their energy and become more stable

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement about a double covalent bond.
questions.explanation: A double covalent bond is represented by two lines (=). (Section 3.2.2)

options: A double covalent bond is formed by the mutual sharing of one electron pair.
A double covalent bond is formed when two atoms share three electrons each.
A double covalent bond is represented by two lines (=).

questions.prompt: Which covalent molecules ionise completely in water and behave as very strong acids?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen chloride, sulphuric acid and nitric acid ionise completely in water.

questions.prompt: Which substance has the formula NaF?
questions.explanation: NaF is the formula of sodium fluoride.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula of sulphur dioxide?
questions.explanation: The formula of sulphur dioxide is SO₂.

questions.prompt: Which of the following situations gives a covalent bond?
questions.explanation: When two hydrogen atoms share their electrons separately with one oxygen atom, a covalent bond is formed.

options: two hydrogen atoms share their electrons separately with one oxygen atom
positive sodium ions are held together by mobile electrons
strong electrostatic attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻

questions.prompt: Which three types of bonds are considered in section 3.2 of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 deals with ionic, covalent and coordinate covalent bonds; the metallic bond is in 3.3.

questions.prompt: What is the structural formula of Hydrogen chloride (HCl)?
questions.explanation: The structural formula of Hydrogen chloride (HCl) is H — Cl.

questions.prompt: Which one of these does NOT describe a single covalent bond correctly?
questions.explanation: That statement is false. A single covalent bond is represented by one line (—). (Section 3.2.2)

options: A single covalent bond joins carbon and nitrogen in hydrogen cyanide.
A single covalent bond is represented by one line (—).
A single covalent bond joins each hydrogen atom to the oxygen atom in a water molecule.

questions.prompt: What kind of ion is Magnesium ion (Mg²⁺)?
questions.explanation: Magnesium ion (Mg²⁺) is a cation. (Section 3.2.1)

questions.prompt: The Ca²⁺ ion has the same electronic configuration as which noble gas?
questions.explanation: Ca²⁺ has the electronic configuration of argon.

questions.prompt: What is the structural formula of Carbon dioxide (CO₂)?
questions.explanation: The structural formula of Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is O = C = O.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a solid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a solid at room temperature. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a correct statement about covalent compounds?
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points. (Section 3.6)

options: Covalent compounds are hydrated by water, whose molecules surround the free ions.
Covalent compounds usually have high melting and boiling points.
Covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a covalent compound?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is a covalent compound. (Section 3.6)

questions.prompt: Which one of these is a use of graphite?
questions.explanation: Graphite is used for industrial lubricants. (Section 3.8)

options: drill bits for drilling through hard rocks in mining

questions.prompt: The Al³⁺ ion has the same electronic configuration as which noble gas?
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ has the electronic configuration of neon.

questions.prompt: Which of these are held together by the strong attraction between mobile electrons and positive ions?
questions.explanation: Metals are held together by the strong attraction between mobile electrons and positive ions. (Section 3.6)

questions.prompt: What is the structural formula of Hydrogen (H₂)?
questions.explanation: The structural formula of Hydrogen (H₂) is H — H.

questions.prompt: Which type of bond is present between the two atoms of a hydrogen molecule?
questions.explanation: A single covalent bond is present between the two atoms of a hydrogen molecule. (Section 3.2.2)

questions.prompt: Which rule says that eight electrons in the outermost shell mean stability?
questions.explanation: Eight outermost electrons give stability and hence unreactivity: the octet rule.

questions.prompt: Which one of these is an example of a metallic bond?
questions.explanation: When positive ions are submerged in a sea of electrons, a metallic bond is formed.

options: a proton accepts a lone pair from the oxygen of a water molecule
positive ions are submerged in a sea of electrons
two hydrogen atoms share their electrons separately with one oxygen atom

questions.prompt: Which free charged particles, if any, are present in Molten calcium chloride?
questions.explanation: Molten calcium chloride conducts electricity because of free ions. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Which free charged particles, if any, are present in Sodium metal?
questions.explanation: Sodium metal conducts electricity because of free electrons. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a use of coal?
questions.explanation: Coal is used for fuel in electricity-generating plants. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Which one of these is a property of an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: An ionic compound has this property: A melting point as high as 801 °C (NaCl). (Section 3.6)

options: Usually soluble in non-polar solvents like benzene
Mostly exists as discrete neutral molecules
A melting point as high as 801 °C (NaCl)

questions.prompt: Which one of these is an anion?
questions.explanation: Bromide ion (Br⁻) is an anion. (Section 3.2.1)

questions.prompt: What type of bonding is present in Methane (CH₄)?
questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) contains covalent bonding. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a correct statement about the coordinate covalent bond?
questions.explanation: The coordinate covalent bond is represented by an arrow head pointing towards the acceptor. (Section 3.2)

options: The coordinate covalent bond is non-directional because the ions are spherical and surround each other from all sides.
The coordinate covalent bond results from atoms losing or gaining electrons to acquire the configuration of the nearest noble gas.
The coordinate covalent bond is represented by an arrow head pointing towards the acceptor.

questions.prompt: Which free charged particles, if any, are present in Graphite?
questions.explanation: Graphite conducts electricity because of free electrons. (Section 3.8)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a property of an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: An ionic compound has this property: Conducts electricity in the molten state. (Section 3.6)

options: Made of two or more non-metals
Conducts electricity in the molten state
Usually soluble in non-polar solvents like benzene

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement about the ionic bond.
questions.explanation: The ionic bond is also called the electrovalent bond. (Section 3.2)

options: The ionic bond breaks with both bonded electrons going to the donor species.
The ionic bond results from the sharing of electrons between atoms so that each acquires the configuration of the nearest noble gas.
The ionic bond is also called the electrovalent bond.

questions.prompt: In which section of the chapter is 'Hydration of ions' discussed?
questions.explanation: 'Hydration of ions' is discussed in section 3.8 Nature of bonding and properties.

options: 3.1 Why do atoms form chemical bonds?

questions.prompt: Which substance has the formula NH₃?
questions.explanation: NH₃ is the formula of ammonia.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of electrons are shared in all the bonds of a molecule of hydrogen cyanide (HCN)?
questions.explanation: A molecule of hydrogen cyanide has 4 shared electron pair(s) in total.

questions.prompt: The Li⁺ ion has the same electronic configuration as which noble gas?
questions.explanation: Li⁺ has the electronic configuration of helium.

questions.prompt: What is the structural formula of Nitrogen (N₂)?
questions.explanation: The structural formula of Nitrogen (N₂) is N ≡ N.

questions.prompt: Which ions remain in solution after AgCl is precipitated from NaCl and AgNO₃?
questions.explanation: Ag⁺ and Cl⁻ form AgCl; Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ stay dissolved.
